issues: Gifting a $1,000-$2,000 sofa as a housewarming gift is highly unusual, though it aligns with the persona's high budget.

The claim of a 'transparent supply chain' is completely unsupported by the advertiser's stated claims. Additionally, this persona is highly skeptical of vague sustainability claims, making this angle ineffective and potentially greenwashing.

config.advertiser_summary: Mid-century modern furniture shipped direct, targeting people in new homes or apartments with premium sofas.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click (verifiable without trusting a pixel). Market price to win a page view on these hosts: $0.83-$1.11 per click (median $0.95), from the simulated auction against the other campaigns. 'balanced' bidding tries to win up to 60% of each host's page views; the planned bid per host is the price that wins its planned share.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: market price $0.82-$1.11 (median $0.95); bidding $0.65 wins ~3% of page views, paying ~$0.62 per click (second price)
market price $0.83-$1.09 (median $0.93); bidding $0.66 wins ~3% of page views, paying ~$0.61 per click (second price)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: planned bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured rates aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: planned bid x pacing x conversion likelihood, up to the ceiling

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget; the ceiling per host is the price that wins your 'balanced' share.
